# SHIBUSDT #89469 near-TP continuation investigation Г?" 2026-10-10

- Status: investigation approved; implementation is explicitly not approved.
  This workstream must not alter or delay FIX-153 release work.
- Hypothesis to test: a breached profit lock close to target may sometimes
  continue when current market structure and momentum remain supportive.
- Important counter-hypothesis: `1h=NEUTRAL` is not positive continuation
  evidence merely because 1m/5m are `WATCH`. Relaxing that guard on distance
  to TP alone could create false holds in weak or sideways markets.
- Required evidence before a policy change: use historical Replay/production
  evidence to compare the current exit rule against a hypothetical bounded
  hold using only information available at the breach. Segment results by
  1h/5m context, regime, trend structure, momentum, retracement depth and
  target-progress band. Evaluate TP hit rate, retained profit, adverse move,
  drawdown, and false-hold frequency. No post-exit price may inform entry or
  exit eligibility.
- Rejected approach: do not authorize continuation from `WATCH/WATCH/NEUTRAL`
  or near-TP distance alone.
- Code-review refinement: `PositionExitPolicy` creates a sharp tier boundary:
  with supportive 5m/current evidence, 1h `WATCH` can hold a breached lock but
  1h `NEUTRAL` falls through to `PROFIT_LOCK_EXIT`. Existing FIX-11T near-TP
  protection arms at 90% target progress and is evaluated after the ordinary
  lock-breach exit, so it could not affect #89469 at 84.28% progress.
- Fee-model refinement: `WalletAutoExecutionService` writes `fee_usdt=0` for
  paper BUY, SELL, and near-TP partial-harvest executions. Any policy Replay
  comparison must add an explicit fee/slippage model before claiming protected
  gross profit is a net gain.
- Approved experiment protocol from independent review: Production policy is
  unchanged. Compare (A) existing immediate lock exit, (B) a one-window,
  near-TP continuation using existing time-safe structure/momentum/context
  calculations, and (C) a volatility-adjusted tighter trailing exit. Use a
  pre-registered 85% TP-progress primary threshold; #89469 at 84.28% does not
  qualify and must not drive threshold selection. Require non-bearish 5m/1h,
  a fee-adjusted protected floor with modeled adverse fills, explicit numeric
  momentum/retracement definitions, no timer resets or repeated extensions,
  and strictly as-of-breach evidence. Evaluate net expectancy, drawdown,
  false-hold/adverse-move rate, and include later-decline counterexamples;
  reserve an out-of-sample period before any implementation decision.
- Final protocol controls: calculate TP progress only from immutable original
  entry and original TP; exclude and report zero/negative/invalid target
  distance. Every A/B/C candidate must use identical historical data,
  evaluation periods, and fee/slippage assumptions. Candidate B must model an
  intrawindow price path sufficiently to determine which of its emergency
  floor or target was reached first; candle high/low alone is not evidence of
  that order. Pre-register the minimum sample size, required net-expectancy
  improvement, and maximum allowed drawdown deterioration before results are
  viewed, then report the qualification count for the B cohort.
- Final cohort and comparison definition: Candidate B is eligible only in the
  85% to strictly-less-than-90% original-TP-progress band, with fresh,
  quality-valid 1h `NEUTRAL`, supportive fresh/quality-valid 5m, and required
  current-frame structure/momentum evidence. Missing, stale, invalid, or
  unknown 1h/5m evidence makes the case ineligible rather than non-bearish.
  This avoids changing or competing with existing FIX-11T behaviour at 90%.
  Pre-count the eligible cohort; insufficient sample means keep collecting.
  B-versus-A is the sole primary comparison; C is secondary/exploratory and
  must have its trailing formula fixed before Replay. Verify ATR, spread, and
  tick-size availability as of breach; if historical spread is unavailable,
  use a declared fixed assumption and sensitivity analysis.
- Final breach semantics: eligibility uses `breach_tp_progress`, calculated
  from the executable price at the exact profit-lock breach, not the historic
  high-water mark. Persist/report both `max_tp_progress` and
  `breach_tp_progress`. The continuation emergency floor is distinct from the
  breached original lock; if actual executable price (including modeled
  fee/spread/slippage) already violates that floor, exit immediately. Freeze
  numerical precision, 90%-boundary precedence (FIX-11T owns 90%+), hold
  length, tolerance, floor, costs, sample threshold, and success criteria
  before inspecting results. Report confidence intervals and chronological
  out-of-sample results; a small qualifying cohort is insufficient evidence.
- Team-2 final validity controls: create and commit a numerical pre-registration
  before any outcome is viewed, recording its immutable content hash here.
  Verify available intrabar path data; where tick/price-event evidence cannot
  order TP versus emergency-floor contact, mark the case ambiguous, apply one
  conservative adverse-move-first rule consistently, and report analyses both
  with and without those cases. Compute the floor per trade as
  `max(original_lock - tolerance, fee_adjusted_breakeven)` and report when
  breakeven binds. Compare A and B as paired outcomes on the same eligible
  breach events, reporting per-event B-minus-A and the count of later declines
  avoided by A.

# Replay-versus-Production parity audit Г?" 2026-10-10

- Scope: source-level comparison of the manual Regression/Replay pipeline with
  the current paper-trading Production path. No trading code, configuration,
  database data, or Replay result was changed.
- Confirmed shared authority: Replay regenerates technical indicators through
  `TechnicalIndicatorService`, signals through `AnalysisService`, BUY authority
  through `ExecutionIntelligenceService`, BUY/SELL validation through
  `TradeExecutionValidationService`, and normal exit, TP-continuation,
  profit-lock, and near-TP policies through the corresponding shared policy
  classes. When canonical `LEGACY`/`APPLIED` price events exist, the Replay
  consumes them in timestamp order before making the same close-candle signal
  visible, matching the documented live ordering.
- Confirmed boundary: Replay is a shadow simulation, not a transactionally
  identical copy of Production. It starts with fixed capital of 10,000 USDT,
  manages one symbol/position in isolation, uses replay-local daily budget and
  position state, and writes only `*_test` tables. It therefore cannot
  reproduce an actual wallet balance, simultaneous positions, global
  `maxOpenPositions`, daily loss limit, idempotency races, database locks, or
  real execution latency.
- Confirmed historical-evidence limitation: derivatives history is not
  persisted, so historical Replay always receives `UNAVAILABLE` derivatives
  context when that feature is enabled. Historical order-book evaluation uses
  stored snapshots only and becomes `UNAVAILABLE` when no snapshot exists,
  whereas live Production samples its in-memory/live Binance source. Such runs
  are useful simulations but are not full signal-parity proof unless the
  required historical evidence exists and is reported.
- Confirmed price-evidence limitation: a Replay run labels itself
  `EXACT_PRICE_REPLAY` whenever at least one accepted price event exists. It
  does not prove complete tick coverage for every time an open position needed
  protection. Windows with no accepted events fall back to signal prices and
  are labelled `SIGNAL_PRICE_FALLBACK`; neither fallback nor partial coverage
  should be described as tick-exact reproduction.
- Test evidence: Java 21 focused tests passed for profit-lock/TP-extension
  parity, position exit/continuation, near-TP policy, and shared sizing.
  Existing Replay-specific coverage is narrow: it does not execute a complete
  Production-versus-Replay scenario across entry, add, wallet controls,
  price-event ordering, partial harvest, and exit.
- Conclusion: Replay is suitable for controlled, manual strategy regression
  and the approved FIX-155 research work only when each run carries explicit
  evidence-quality labels. It is not yet valid to claim it is fully identical
  to Production in all phases. A future parity program must add deterministic
  scenario tests and a run-level eligibility contract before using Replay as a
  release-equivalence certificate.


===== codex-docs/TRADING_RULES.md =====
# FIX-154 higher-timeframe BUY rule Г?" 2026-10-10

- `data_quality_valid=true` is required before a bearish 1h signal can be
  treated as trusted. `NULL` is unknown and fails closed for bearish evidence.
- A trusted `STRONG_SELL` at `confidence_score >= 70` blocks the BUY.
- A trusted `SELL`, or trusted `STRONG_SELL` below 70, is a SOFT conflict:
  profiles receive effective 1h `NEUTRAL`, and any allowed initial BUY is
  capped at 25%.
- A bearish 5m still returns `5M_BEARISH_VETO` before any 1h result.
- Existing progressive/add rules retain their raw 1h requirement; a SOFT 1h
  never authorizes an add.

# FIX-153 candle continuity rule Г?" 2026-10-10

- Missing price evidence never becomes invented OHLCV data and never bypasses
  the data-quality gate.
- Automatic reconciliation may restore only one exact, final Binance candle.
  Its recovered/backfilled row has no close token and cannot directly cause
  analysis, a signal, or a trade.
- A later normal live close is the only route that resumes ordinary signal
  generation after a repaired quality window.

# 2026-10-08 Г?" FIX-153 local-candle hardening status

- Implemented: OFF-mode trader-owned candle ingestion, monotonic close tokens,
  bounded detector/lanes, canonical price evidence, direct-attempt freshness,
  REST exchange-time close validation, and controlled ADMIN drain behavior.
- Operational impact: a successful drain exits the JVM; a timeout resumes
  admission. Price protection pauses during a drain window.
- Database impact: existing FIX-153 V106/B105 schema remains required; no
  production migration or data change was run by Codex.
- Release status: NOT APPROVED FOR PRODUCTION. Java 21, disposable-MySQL,
  crash/race, Windows lock, soak and Replay-parity validation remain open.

# 2026-10-08 Г?" FIX-153 exchange/database clock correction

- Problem: JVM/database clock skew could make a Binance-derived candle appear
  too early or too old during freshness checks.
- Solution: `ExchangeClockSynchronizer` measures Binance server time against
  database UTC and JVM time at startup and periodically; database and JVM
  callers apply their own bounded offset without HTTP inside locks.
- The clock-skew warning uses the larger absolute database or JVM offset; the
  dedicated Binance time client has a five-second connect/read bound.
- General Binance REST requests now use the configured request timeout, and
  scheduled clock sampling cannot monopolise the four-thread scheduler pool.
- Bootstrap REST reads occur before its local candle-write transaction, so
  the bounded Binance timeout does not hold a database transaction open.

# 2026-10-09 Г?" FIX-153 audit: analysis outcomes and protection clock

- Audit result: normal live and historical analysis persist a `TradeSignal`,
  including neutral/no-entry decisions; there is no normal analysed-without-
  durable-outcome path to reconcile.
- Corrected the post-lock direct-protection timestamp validation to use the
  JVM-to-exchange clock correction, matching initial receipt validation.
- A universal shutdown barrier remains a separate, unverified design task:
  it must cover financial mutations without treating unrelated administration
  or configuration writes as trading authority.
- Database impact: none. Production and Replay impact: execution freshness now
  follows an automatically measured exchange-aligned reference clock.
- Validation still required: unavailable-time-source, stale observation,
  positive/negative skew, and first-attempt freshness regression tests.

  `FIX-146` to `FIX-154` in the project guidance and architecture record.
- It remains separate from FIX-153, unimplemented, and not approved for

# FIX-154 higher-timeframe BUY rule ƒ?" 2026-10-10

  treated as trusted. `NULL` is unknown and fails closed for bearish evidence.

  never authorizes an add.

  Its recovered/backfilled row has no close token and cannot directly cause
  analysis, a signal, or a trade.
- A later normal live close is the only route that resumes ordinary signal
  generation after a repaired quality window.

===== codex-docs/ARCHITECTURE.md lines 1-100 =====
# Crypto AI Trader ƒ?" Architecture

Status labels used in this document:

- **Current** ƒ?" present in the repository today.
- **Pending** ƒ?" approved design direction, not implemented or deployed.
- **Legacy/shared** ƒ?" existing shared-market path retained as historical evidence
  while the trader moves to local-candle ownership.

## Current release status

**FIX-153 is implemented in source but is NOT APPROVED FOR PRODUCTION.**
It moves the trader toward collector-free, trader-owned local candle ingestion
in `shared-market.mode=OFF`. Java 21, disposable-MySQL, crash/race, Windows
two-process, soak, OFF-mode and Replay-parity proof gates remain open.

FIX-154 is a separate pending higher-timeframe design. It is not implemented
and is not part of FIX-153 deployment scope.

## System purpose

The application is a Spring Boot cryptocurrency trader that analyses Binance
market data, persists candles and technical indicators, creates trade signals,
and performs paper-wallet execution and position protection. Production and
Replay are intended to use equivalent persisted market evidence.

## Runtime and data ownership

| Area | Current ownership | Target direction |
|---|---|---|
| Trader database | `crypto_ai` | Remains the trader's only runtime database. |
| Collector database | `crypto_ai_v2` | Collector remains separate and is not read/written by the trader at runtime. |
| Candle ingestion | In OFF mode, trader-owned Binance ingestion writes local `crypto_ai.candle`. | Must be proven in a collector-free deployment rehearsal. |
| Candle processing | Bounded lanes, close-transition tokens and a local detector are implemented. | MySQL/race/crash proof remains required. |
| Trading | Paper wallet and managed positions. | Live-exchange orders are outside the local-candle automatic-resolution design. |

## Current primary flow

```text
Binance WebSocket kline
  -> BinanceKlineService
  -> KlineTransactionCoordinator
      -> input transaction: candle + canonical 1m market price event
      -> protection transaction: LivePositionProtectionService
      -> observer transaction
      -> close-dispatch transaction
  -> CandleClosedEvent (AFTER_COMMIT)
  -> CandleAnalysisDispatcher
  -> CandleClosedAnalysisWorker
  -> TechnicalIndicatorService
  -> AnalysisService / TradeSignal
  -> SignalProcessingCoordinator
  -> PaperTradingService / wallet and managed-position state
```

`KlineTransactionCoordinator` preserves input -> protection -> observer ->
close-dispatch ordering. Closed-candle analysis is asynchronous and must not
run on the Binance ingestion thread.

## Current core persistence

| Table/domain | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `candle` | Local OHLCV candle history keyed by symbol, interval, and open time. |
| `technical_indicator` | Persisted indicator snapshots derived from closed candles. |
| `trade_signal` | Persisted analysis decisions and their context. |
| `signal_processing_work` | Durable processing registration/status for a persisted signal. |
| `market_price_event` | Canonical 1m price evidence used by protection and Replay. |
| Paper wallet / position tables | Paper executions, open-position state, TP/SL/profit protection. |

## Legacy/shared-market path

**Current but pending retirement from the trader runtime.**

The shared path includes `SharedMarketSource`, `SharedMarketConsumer`,
`SharedAnalysisDispatcher`, cutover/readiness logic, and local historical
tables such as `shared_market_event_delivery`, `shared_market_consumer_state`,
and `shared_market_health`. These records remain evidence and must not be
dropped, reset, or used to manufacture an approval.

The collector event/cursor source is `crypto_ai_v2.market_data_stream_event`
and `market_data_stream_cursor`. In the target local-candle runtime, the
trader must not connect to, read, or write these collector tables.

`V103__fix_149_fresh_admission_indexes` is an existing Java Flyway migration
that requires the collector event table for a fresh installation. A trader-only
bootstrap policy is therefore **pending** and remains a release blocker. Do
not edit applied Flyway migrations or Flyway history.

## Implemented, unverified: local-candle architecture (FIX-153)

The implemented intended mode is `shared-market.mode=OFF` with trader-owned Binance kline
ingestion and local candle writes. The shared executors and direct-ingestion
path must never run together.

Implemented safeguards:

- Candle writes are monotonic: a late open update cannot reopen or overwrite a
  closed candle.
- A closed-candle transition is admitted exactly once using an atomic upsert

===== codex-docs/ARCHITECTURE.md lines 101-200 =====
  result plus in-process admission coordination.
- A bounded local detector recovers a closed candle that was committed before
  the in-memory event/dispatcher could start analysis.
- Fresh candles may execute; stale candles are analysed historically only, or
  their already-owned work is expired without business execution.
- Analysis lanes are bounded. Under overload, 1m may retain only the latest
  pending candle; higher intervals use an explicit bounded FIFO policy.
- Historic shared `REVIEW_REQUIRED` evidence must not block OFF-mode work.
- OFF-mode health/admin endpoints must use local-candle health and must not
  query retired shared-market tables.
- Current REST backfill can finalise an interrupted open row but cannot mint a
  runtime close token or dispatch analysis. Runtime close tokens plus
  provenance keep backfill out of detector admission. The approved, pending
  automatic-reconciliation extension will also insert an exact wholly absent
  candle only inside the active quality window, with `BACKFILL` provenance and
  the same no-token/no-dispatch boundary.
- Observed local behavior (2026-10-09): a WebSocket reconnect at a candle-close
  boundary can leave the already-persisted 1m/5m rows open because Binance does
  not replay the final closed-kline event. The current detector recovers missing
  analysis admission, not missing close facts. An authoritative, bounded REST
  repair may therefore finalise the exact `closed=0` row or, under the approved
  gap-backfill scope, insert an exact absent identity. It must preserve existing
  provenance, use `BACKFILL` for an insertion, create no close-transition token,
  and never dispatch historical work. Automatic reconciliation of this reconnect
  case remains a FIX-153 release gate; the one-time local repair is evidence,
  not proof that the gap is closed.
- Approved pending reconciliation design: gap backfill is insert-only (no
  duplicate-key update); it can never alter a live row that appears during a
  REST request. Candidate selection is bounded to the active quality window;
  terminal audit records are not retried. Every candle/work route must produce
  a durable terminal outcome or remain explicitly retryable after a transient
  failure. Historical-only processing has no execution authority.
- The pending universal mutation barrier is an in-memory drain participant,
  not a database or persistent trading fence. Outside drain it must not delay,
  queue, or block fresh trading, signals, or protection. Open-position
  protection during application replacement remains an unresolved release gate.
- Local source now contains the first reconciliation implementation slice:
  V107 durable audit/outcome tables, update-only authoritative open-row repair,
  pure insert-only gap backfill, a dedicated recovery executor, a reconnect
  request hook, and drain participation. It is disabled by default and remains
  unvalidated on MySQL; it has no deployment approval.
- Direct prices are normalised to `DECIMAL(30,12)` before persistence,
  protection and completion. Equal timestamps have one canonical receipt.
- Every processing attempt is freshness-checked after normal locks using the
  database-to-exchange correction. JVM-origin timestamp decisions use the
  separately measured JVM-to-exchange correction. The measurement performs no
  HTTP under execution locks and uses a bounded five-second time-only client.
  General Binance REST calls use the configured request timeout, and scheduled
  clock sampling has a four-thread Spring scheduler pool.
  Bootstrap obtains time/klines before opening its local candle-write
  transaction, so a stalled REST request does not retain database resources.
  REST bootstrap gets Binance server time before klines.
- An ADMIN-only drain stops analysis admission, exits the JVM on successful
  quiesce, and resumes admission on timeout. Price protection pauses during
  the controlled drain window.

## Implemented, unverified: protection price-event state machine

For direct 1m price observations, the target evidence lifecycle is:

```text
PENDING
  -> APPLIED                 (protection effects and state commit together)
  -> NON_CANONICAL           (invalid, stale, out-of-order, or duplicate)
  -> PROTECTION_NOT_APPLIED  (confirmed rollback/crash resolution)
```

Replay and price authority consume only accepted `LEGACY`/`APPLIED` rows.
Replay must reject a parity claim when the requested range contains unresolved
direct `PENDING` evidence; this must not block live trading.

The automatic resolver is valid only for the paper-trading phase, where every
protection effect commits in the same transaction as its `APPLIED` update.
Before deployment, the code must prove that there are no asynchronous,
`REQUIRES_NEW`, in-memory-only, or external effects in this boundary. A future
live-exchange order needs a separate idempotent/exchange-reconciliation design.

The target runtime also requires exactly one active trader process. This is an
operational prerequisite, not a database lease or fence.

## Pending: FIX-154 higher-timeframe BUY validation

FIX-154 is separate from the local-candle change and is not implemented.

Its purpose is to let a historical bearish 1h signal affect a current 1m BUY
only when the historical evidence is fresh, quality-valid, and sufficiently
strong. `btcContextEntryAllowed=false` on a historical signal is investigatory
evidence, not a higher-timeframe quality gate; the current 1m BTC protection
remains unchanged.

The design includes reliability bands (`NOT_TRUSTED`, `SOFT_CONFLICT`,
`HARD_BEARISH_CANDIDATE`), required fresh/quality-valid bearish 5m support for
a hard veto, persisted `trade_signal.data_quality_valid`, recovery release
rules, immutable outcome audit evidence, and Replay/no-look-ahead parity.

The implementation design is maintained in `codex-docs/FIX-154_TECHNICAL_DESIGN.md`.
It supersedes no existing deployed behavior and is deliberately separate from
the unrelated legacy readiness document under `src/main/resources/md/FIX-146.md`.

## Deployment posture

Neither FIX-153 nor FIX-154 is deployment-ready. FIX-153 source hardening is
implemented but unverified; FIX-154 remains pending.

Required validation includes Java 21 build/tests, disposable MySQL bootstrap,
real-MySQL concurrency and lock-wait tests, crash/restart tests, stale-input
tests, Replay parity checks, OFF-mode health/admin checks, collector-free
runtime verification, deterministic dispatcher/detector/drain tests,
two-process Windows lock rehearsal, and sustained-load observation across
enabled symbols and intervals. This local workspace has Java 17 and cannot
compile the Java 21 project.

No production configuration, database, service, or deployment change is made
without explicit user approval.

## FIX-153 validation status (2026-10-09)

The reconciliation component now has deterministic Java 21 coverage for its
core admission and outcome contract. The tests execute the real audit and
outcome stores against H2 while mocking only Binance and the candle write
boundary. They prove that healthy delayed live closes are not taken over and
that recovery remains token-free/non-live when it is positively evidenced.

The real-MySQL suite contains matching update-only and insert-only assertions,
but it requires a deliberately disposable loopback MySQL instance and is not
run by the ordinary unit-test goal. This is a release gate, not a warning that
can be waived. The shared Binance 429/418 admission gate, universal mutation
barrier, structural historical-only isolation, financial-effect reconciler,
atomicity/crash proofs, replacement-time position protection, Replay parity,
and soak validation remain incomplete. Therefore `local-candle.reconciliation.enabled`
must stay `false`.

The single `local-candle` configuration mapping is a startup invariant. It now
contains both reconciliation and existing local-runtime properties; a second
mapping is invalid YAML and prevents the Spring application context from
starting.

### Shared Binance REST admission

`BinanceRestAdmissionGate` owns one process-wide REST cooldown. It is consulted
immediately before every call through `BinanceMarketDataClient`; a 429/418
response extends the cooldown using `Retry-After` when it is supplied, otherwise
the bounded fallback. This protects all local REST consumers from repeatedly
calling Binance during a rate-limit/ban response. It is deliberately not part
of the WebSocket or protection path and is not a persisted trading fence.

### Outcome-schema startup invariant

The active signal-processing runtime writes `candle_analysis_outcome` for
terminal analysis evidence. V108 therefore ships with the FIX-154 release even
though local-candle reconciliation remains disabled. `CandleAnalysisOutcomeSchemaVerifier`
runs after Flyway and fails application startup with a clear message if the
table is absent; this prevents later processing transactions from failing only
when they attempt their first outcome write.
# FIX-154 implementation update ƒ?" 2026-10-10

`HigherTimeframeBuyAssessmentService` is the single pure assessment boundary for
the 5m/1h BUY context. It returns effective decisions separately from the JPA
entities, so a SOFT 1h conflict can be assessed as effective `NEUTRAL` without
ever changing the persisted signal. `TradeExecutionValidationService` uses it
for direct BUY and accumulated-evidence authority; `OpportunityConsolidationService`
uses the same assessment for consolidation. A trusted SOFT bearish 1h limits an
initial entry to 25%; a trusted HARD or unknown bearish 1h rejects it, while
the legacy 5m bearish veto keeps priority.

`buy_htf_assessment_audit` is append-only operational evidence. Its writer is
best-effort and uses a bounded dedicated executor: auditing never borrows an
execution transaction's database connection, is skipped in Replay, and cannot
be part of a BUY decision. The progressive add route retains its
existing raw-1h guard; it writes `SOFT_HTF_ADD_BLOCKED` evidence only after
that guard has already rejected an add.

`GET /api/fix154/health` exposes non-gating counters for untrusted bearish
blocks, soft caps, soft add blocks, and best-effort audit failures.

## FIX-153 automatic local-candle reconciliation ƒ?" enabled 2026-10-10

In `shared-market.mode=OFF`, `LocalCandleReconciliationService` runs every
five seconds on its dedicated single-worker executor. It finds eligible
missing or interrupted candle identities inside the data-quality window, reads
the authoritative Binance candle, and writes only verified final evidence.
An existing open row is finalized by an update-only path; a missing row uses a
plain insert-if-absent backfill path. Neither route creates a close token,
dispatches analysis, or executes a trade. The next genuine live close resumes
ordinary analysis after the quality window is complete.

# SHIBUSDT #89469 near-TP continuation investigation Г?" 2026-10-10

- Status: investigation approved; implementation is explicitly not approved.
  This workstream must not alter or delay FIX-153 release work.
- Hypothesis to test: a breached profit lock close to target may sometimes
  continue when current market structure and momentum remain supportive.
- Important counter-hypothesis: `1h=NEUTRAL` is not positive continuation
  evidence merely because 1m/5m are `WATCH`. Relaxing that guard on distance
  to TP alone could create false holds in weak or sideways markets.
- Required evidence before a policy change: use historical Replay/production
  evidence to compare the current exit rule against a hypothetical bounded
  hold using only information available at the breach. Segment results by
  1h/5m context, regime, trend structure, momentum, retracement depth and
  target-progress band. Evaluate TP hit rate, retained profit, adverse move,
  drawdown, and false-hold frequency. No post-exit price may inform entry or
  exit eligibility.
- Rejected approach: do not authorize continuation from `WATCH/WATCH/NEUTRAL`
  or near-TP distance alone.
- Code-review refinement: `PositionExitPolicy` creates a sharp tier boundary:
  with supportive 5m/current evidence, 1h `WATCH` can hold a breached lock but

  1h `NEUTRAL` falls through to `PROFIT_LOCK_EXIT`. Existing FIX-11T near-TP
  protection arms at 90% target progress and is evaluated after the ordinary
  lock-breach exit, so it could not affect #89469 at 84.28% progress.

  paper BUY, SELL, and near-TP partial-harvest executions. Any policy Replay
  comparison must add an explicit fee/slippage model before claiming protected
  gross profit is a net gain.
- Approved experiment protocol from independent review: Production policy is
  unchanged. Compare (A) existing immediate lock exit, (B) a one-window,
  near-TP continuation using existing time-safe structure/momentum/context
  calculations, and (C) a volatility-adjusted tighter trailing exit. Use a

  qualify and must not drive threshold selection. Require non-bearish 5m/1h,

  evaluation periods, and fee/slippage assumptions. Candidate B must model an

  current-frame structure/momentum evidence. Missing, stale, invalid, or

# Replay-versus-Production parity audit Г?" 2026-10-10

- Scope: source-level comparison of the manual Regression/Replay pipeline with
  the current paper-trading Production path. No trading code, configuration,
  database data, or Replay result was changed.
- Confirmed shared authority: Replay regenerates technical indicators through
  `TechnicalIndicatorService`, signals through `AnalysisService`, BUY authority
  through `ExecutionIntelligenceService`, BUY/SELL validation through
  `TradeExecutionValidationService`, and normal exit, TP-continuation,
  profit-lock, and near-TP policies through the corresponding shared policy
  classes. When canonical `LEGACY`/`APPLIED` price events exist, the Replay
  consumes them in timestamp order before making the same close-candle signal
  visible, matching the documented live ordering.
- Confirmed boundary: Replay is a shadow simulation, not a transactionally
  identical copy of Production. It starts with fixed capital of 10,000 USDT,
  manages one symbol/position in isolation, uses replay-local daily budget and
  position state, and writes only `*_test` tables. It therefore cannot
  reproduce an actual wallet balance, simultaneous positions, global
  `maxOpenPositions`, daily loss limit, idempotency races, database locks, or
  real execution latency.
- Confirmed historical-evidence limitation: derivatives history is not
  persisted, so historical Replay always receives `UNAVAILABLE` derivatives
  context when that feature is enabled. Historical order-book evaluation uses
  stored snapshots only and becomes `UNAVAILABLE` when no snapshot exists,
  whereas live Production samples its in-memory/live Binance source. Such runs
  are useful simulations but are not full signal-parity proof unless the
  required historical evidence exists and is reported.
- Confirmed price-evidence limitation: a Replay run labels itself
  `EXACT_PRICE_REPLAY` whenever at least one accepted price event exists. It
  does not prove complete tick coverage for every time an open position needed
  protection. Windows with no accepted events fall back to signal prices and
  are labelled `SIGNAL_PRICE_FALLBACK`; neither fallback nor partial coverage
  should be described as tick-exact reproduction.
- Test evidence: Java 21 focused tests passed for profit-lock/TP-extension
  parity, position exit/continuation, near-TP policy, and shared sizing.
  Existing Replay-specific coverage is narrow: it does not execute a complete
  Production-versus-Replay scenario across entry, add, wallet controls,
  price-event ordering, partial harvest, and exit.
- Conclusion: Replay is suitable for controlled, manual strategy regression
  and the approved FIX-155 research work only when each run carries explicit
  evidence-quality labels. It is not yet valid to claim it is fully identical
  to Production in all phases. A future parity program must add deterministic
  scenario tests and a run-level eligibility contract before using Replay as a
  release-equivalence certificate.

===== SPEC OUTLINE =====
1:# FIX-156 — Replay / Production Business-Logic Parity
12:## 1. Decision and non-negotiable scope
22:| `ANALYSIS_PARITY` | A stored Production signal/outcome is reproducible under the defined as-of evidence and oracle contract. It makes no account/lifecycle claim. |
28:## 2. Explicit Replay boundary
32:They must not read or write any Production account table: `wallet_asset`, `wallet_trade`, `wallet_managed_position`, `paper_position`, `wallet_settings`, account snapshots, daily-account statistics, or live execution state. They must not invoke Binance/HTTP clients or call a Production fallback branch. A run-scoped guard propagates to all Replay child threads and fails closed with `REPLAY_FORBIDDEN_DEPENDENCY` before publication.
38:## 3. Evidence contract and time model
40:### 3.1 Allowed evidence
50:| sentiment/fundamental tables | analysis input only | require collection/availability time and versioned provider/config snapshot; otherwise refuse `ANALYSIS_PARITY`. |
52:`NON_CANONICAL`, `PROTECTION_NOT_APPLIED`, `PENDING`, and uncertain price events are excluded. No future candle, price, signal, configuration, provider-health value, or account state may be used.
54:### 3.2 Candle and signal eligibility
60:### 3.3 Price coverage and fill policy
62:For a comparable decision output, each position-dependent decision span requires fresh accepted price evidence. Source check: Production resolves execution prices (entries and progressive adds) in `ExecutionPriceAuthorityService.resolve`, which accepts a price only if it is no older than `MAX_EXECUTION_PRICE_AGE`, 15 seconds. The Replay-scope branch of the same method applies the same 15-second limit to the Replay price timeline. That rule covers entry and add prices only. E02 must state which freshness rule governs protection (exit) spans, because the protection price stream is filtered by event status, not by this 15-second limit. A span with no usable price event is refused; it is never silently represented by one `EXACT_PRICE_REPLAY` flag for the entire run.
66:The existing signal-price fallback is removed from the Replay baseline. It is reachable only for runs with **zero** price events, and does not execute the full Production exit order. Tests must use the actual Production signal-path sequence: advisory position management, TP, stop loss, rebase floor, profit lock, normal SELL validation, near-TP, then add suppression/handling as applicable. No rule order may be invented from the old Replay fallback.
68:### 3.4 Known Production/Replay differences register (source comparison)
74:| D01 | SELL signals that can close a position | SELL or STRONG_SELL on 1m, 5m or 1h, through `validateSell` | Only 1m SELL or STRONG_SELL | Replay change |
75:| D02 | Profit-lock suppression of SELL signals | Active profit lock ignores the SELL and holds | No such check before `validateSell` (confirmed by two independent source reads) | Replay change |
76:| D03 | Exits at the signal price | Signal path also checks TP, profit lock, stop loss, hard floor at the candle's signal price | Skipped in exact-price mode | Replay change, or proof that the price stream always acts first |
77:| D04 | TP at signal price | Closes as TAKE_PROFIT directly, no continuation or extension | Not evaluated at signal price | Same as D03 |
78:| D05 | Signal visibility to the price stream | Newest stored signal at processing time | Visible from `generatedAt` | Measure `created_at` minus `generated_at` per interval; use Production's availability time |
79:| D06 | Near-TP clock | `Instant.now()` at processing | Price event `observedAt` | One declared rule plus measured outcome impact |
80:| D07 | Entry price | Fresh price resolved at `Instant.now()` | Resolved at the signal's `generatedAt` | Same as D06 |
81:| D08 | Entry wake-up | Setup and confirmed-setup wake-ups tried on every signal | Wake-ups only on 5m; 1m goes to `evaluateBuy` | Verify whether the wake-up can fire on 1m; Replay change if so |
82:| D09 | Progressive adds | Only on 1m and only without an active profit lock (`PaperTradingService`); `evaluateBuy` is not called while the lock is active, so opportunity memory is not touched | No profit-lock check on the add path (confirmed by two independent source reads) | Replay change: skip the add evaluation while the lock is active |
83:| D10 | Failed mechanical exit | `executeMechanicalExit` can return false and the position stays open | Always exits | Declared non-comparable (wallet-driven) |
84:| D11 | Near-TP partial harvest skip | Skipped below Binance minimum for the real quantity | Same check, fixed-notional quantity | Declared non-comparable (quantity-driven) |
85:| D12 | Replay-only logic | None | Zero-event signal-price fallback, FIX-11K and FIX-11Q observers, run-wide exact/fallback boolean | Remove (Section 5.1) |
86:| D13 | Wallet inputs | Real wallet | `wallet_settings`, cash, daily budget, max positions, sizing | Remove (Section 4) |
87:| D14 | Profit-lock calculation | `DynamicProfitLockService.evaluatePrice`, persists state | Replay-local `profitLockState` over `ProfitLockPolicy` | Not yet compared; E02 must show equal outputs on shared fixtures |
88:| D15 | Same-timestamp signal order | Order of arrival at the processing queue | Sorted by `generatedAt`, then 1h, 5m, 1m (`intervalOrder`) | Declared rule; E07 measures how often signals share a timestamp and whether arrival order differed |
89:| D16 | Fallback exit order (`evaluateExit`) | Signal path order: TP, profit lock, stop loss, hard floor, SELL (suppressed while the profit lock is active). No normal HTF exit on the signal path | Fallback order: TP, stop loss, rebase floor, profit lock, normal HTF exit, then 1m `validateSell` | Remove with D12; do not reuse this order anywhere in the baseline |
90:| D17 | Experimental-only branches inside Production classes | `RegimeStateService.apply` returns the detected regime at once; `EntryAuthorityService.evaluate` always returns the normal decision | When an `EXPERIMENTAL` scope is active: N-candle regime persistence, and a breakout-transition probe capped near 25% | Not reachable today (both Replay entry points open the scope in `PRODUCTION_PARITY` mode; only a test opens `EXPERIMENTAL`). Keep unreachable and prove it with a guard test. Production cleanup is out of scope for FIX-156 |
91:| D18 | Replay-aware as-of branches in shared Production classes | Read the database at decision time | Read the Replay timeline when a scope is active: `BtcMarketContextService`, `MultiTimeframeConfluenceService`, `OpportunityConsolidationService`, `ExecutionIntelligenceService` (opportunity memory), `TradeExecutionValidationService`, `ExecutionPriceAuthorityService`, `EntryConsumptionPolicy`, `BuyHtfAssessmentAuditStore` (skips writes) | Not retired. E02 must show equivalent output on shared fixtures. `EntryConsumptionPolicy` depends on whether a BUY executed in the wallet, so in a Replay seeded at Production's recorded entries it must follow Production's recorded executions, not Replay's own |
92:| D19 | Replay-only profilers | None | `ReplayFreshSignalProfiler` (FIX-11L) and `analysisService.beginReplayAnalysisProfiling` (FIX-11M) | Declared observation-only. Baseline run must show identical output with them on and off, or disable them |
93:| D20 | Entry time | `openedAt`, `executedAt` and the managed position's `openedAt` are `Instant.now()` at execution | In-memory `entryTime` is the signal's `generatedAt`; the stored Replay rows use the fresh price's `observedAt`. The two disagree, and for a 5m wake-up the in-memory time can be up to 45 seconds before the trigger. It feeds the rule that decides whether a signal price may be used after entry | Replay change: one entry time, taken from Production's recorded execution time |
94:| D21 | Opportunity state after an add | `markExecuted` is called with the decision from before price revalidation | Called with the revalidated decision | Replay change (small): pass the same decision object as Production |
95:| D22 | Profit-lock enable flag on TP extension | `onTakeProfitExtended` evaluates with the lock enabled | `rebaseForExtendedTarget` passes the admin toggle `isDynamicProfitLockEnabled()` | Replay change (edge case when the toggle is off) |
96:| D23 | Advisory position management | `PositionManagementService.analyze(signal)` runs first on every signal and can apply a position stop loss | Not mirrored; Replay never calls it | Verify in E02 whether it can close a position that the price stream would not; Replay change if so |
97:| D24 | Run-time configuration | Profit-lock percentages and toggles are read from `wallet_settings` row 1 at each evaluation | The same row is read at Replay time, so a settings change after the original decision silently changes Replay | Profile must carry the settings in force at the original decision time; refuse when the history is not available |
98:| D25 | Final price-event tail | Production evaluates protection callbacks regardless of whether another signal is generated | Replay consumes price events only before each generated signal; after the final signal it marks an open position from the final signal price without processing remaining events through `executionEnd` | Replay change: drain the qualified canonical price-event tail through `executionEnd`, or refuse lifecycle parity for an incomplete final span |
99:| D26 | Replay chart endpoint reads Production account table | Production `wallet_trade` is account state | `RegressionTestController` maps `/runs/{id}/all-trades-chart` to `RegressionTestService.allTradesChart(...)`, which queries executed `wallet_trade` rows by symbol/window and returns them as `productionExecutions` beside Replay output | Replay change: remove the account query from the Replay request path. Any comparison overlay comes only from a separately prepared immutable fixture/evidence dataset (E09), labelled non-Replay display evidence. Fixture test: the endpoint issues no query against `wallet_trade`, `paper_position`, or `wallet_settings`. |
100:| D27 | Position still open when the window ends | The position continues and may exit after `executionEnd` | Replay does not close it; it marks the position to the last signal price in the run summary | Classify the lifecycle as censored (outcome unknown). Exclude it from exit-agreement metrics, count and report it separately, and never count it as a match. |
102:### 3.5 Signal-generation differences register (source comparison)
108:| S01 | Signal clock | Live `generatedAt` is `Instant.now()` a short time after the candle close; recovery uses the close time | `evaluationTime = open time + interval` | Non-comparable for live-origin rows, or allow a measured latency tolerance |
109:| S02 | Higher-timeframe and BTC context | Read from the database at processing time; which same-minute signals exist is a race between workers | Read from the Replay timeline; at a given close the 1m always sees the 5m, 1h and BTC signals of that close | Non-comparable; Replay is a deterministic idealisation |
110:| S03 | Derivatives positioning | Live Binance futures call, not persisted | Historical mode returns unavailable or not applicable; error-path confidence adjustment is -10 in Production and 0 in Replay | Non-comparable |
111:| S04 | Order book / liquidity | In-memory samples, live fetch when empty | Persisted observations in the window; unavailable when none, where Production returns insufficient-data hold | Equivalent only where persisted sample rate matches the live window; otherwise non-comparable |
112:| S05 | Previous indicator snapshot | Stored `technical_indicator` row for the previous candle | Same query, but the current snapshot is recomputed and never stored | Replay change: pass a previous snapshot recomputed from the dataset; or equivalent on fixtures from the same code version |
113:| S06 | Data-quality gate | Candle-close worker validates the latest 210 closed candles (gaps, invalid OHLC) and skips the signal; backfilled candles are not analysed | No such gate; Replay analyses every candle in the database | Replay change if row-set parity matters; otherwise report extra rows as non-comparable |
114:| S07 | Open (unclosed) candles | Only closed candles | The helper that lists candles for the timeline has no closed filter; the dataset loader does filter. Which one feeds the timeline was not fully traced | Verify in E08; Replay change: filter to closed candles |
115:| S08 | Signal metadata | `signal_mode` is LIVE, RECOVERY_EXECUTABLE or HISTORICAL_ONLY; `created_at` is set on insert | `analyzeForRegression` never sets `signal_mode`; test row has no `created_at` | Replay change, or exclude these columns from the comparison |
116:| S09 | Sentiment | Provider health and configuration at decision time | Provider weights and flags read at Replay time; every Replay signal counts as historical | Non-comparable unless provider health and configuration history are persisted |
117:| S10 | Intervals | Production analyses whatever intervals are configured, possibly including 15m, 4h and 1d | Replay timeline holds only 1m, 5m and 1h (verified); context from other intervals is missing | Verify the configured intervals in E08; Replay change or non-comparable |
118:| S11 | Warm-up | Full signal history | 3 hours of seeded context | Compare only rows after the warm-up, or lengthen it |
119:| S12 | Configuration | Scoring, BTC, sentiment, fundamental, derivatives and order-book properties as deployed at the time | The same properties as deployed now | Non-comparable unless configuration is versioned (profile fingerprint) |
120:| S13 | Comparison tooling | n/a | `ReplayParityValidator` is not called anywhere in the source (verified). It compares 13 fields and omits scores, stop loss, take profit, price, decision path, time and quality fields. The worker's pass criteria are counts and cadence, not field parity against Production | New comparison component required; this is the 99% metric tool, not a refinement of an existing one |
121:| S14 | Run pass condition | n/a | `RegressionTestWorker` computes `passed = cadencePass && authorityPass && generationPass && livePriceParityPass`, and `livePriceParityPass` is `!productionPriceEvents.isEmpty()` (verified, lines 319 to 323). One price event anywhere makes the price condition true | Replace with per-span coverage qualification (Section 3.3); the flag must never grant a parity label |

202:### 6.2 Required schema and configuration changes
222:## 7. Earned parity algorithm
224:`ANALYSIS_PARITY` is earned only when the frozen source/config policy identity matches, all mandatory as-of evidence exists, candle/data-quality/signal-mode timing passes, and the validator compares the versioned mandatory field set (decision, raw/effective confidence, context/statuses, regime, strategy, entry permission, reason and outcome). Tolerances must be documented and versioned; missing liquidity, derivatives or sentiment uses the stored Production output, not a new live/historical approximation.

# FIX-156 ƒ?" Replay / Production Business-Logic Parity

**Revision:** RPR-0.9.4-DRAFT (RPR-0.9.3-DRAFT with the second-review D26 account-table finding adopted and the censored-lifecycle row renumbered D27; changes listed in Appendix B)  
**Status:** NOT APPROVED ƒ?" IMPLEMENTATION FORBIDDEN  
**Date:** 2026-10-10  
**Code compared:** `d66c7a79-src.zip` (SHA-256 `cbdab04093a8a569c45ddb685ffcae082fab0df5ed928f50d2b185cbcdf5910f`, 651 files) and `cdbf3bd4-src.zip` (SHA-256 `a4a9c494117be24ff55e334bdbda175fe0e17aea2bbe510723519bc1163e9938`, 654 files). Directory comparison: all Java, SQL, resource and POM files are identical; the second package differs only in four script files (three new failed-trade study scripts and one changed status script). Every register row below therefore holds for both packages. Source read only.  
**Review basis:** 12-round Codex/Claude review run `20261010-182733`.  
**Baseline to freeze before approval:** source, configuration, migrations, and complete worktree SHA-256.  

**Current-local-source amendment (2026-10-11):** D25 was verified in `ShadowProductionReplayService` in both `d66c7a79-src.zip` and `cdbf3bd4-src.zip`. It must be re-verified against the package frozen for implementation.

## 1. Decision and non-negotiable scope

This revision adopts the user's existing direction: **FIX-156 changes Replay only. Production source code, behaviour, database writes, account state, HTTP traffic, schedulers, and latency must remain unchanged.** No shared-service extraction is authorised in this fix.

Replay is a manual, single-symbol research tool. It produces traceable decision, position, and exit output at a fixed notionalƒ?"not a wallet, balance, cash reserve, sizing ledger, daily budget, or account simulation. It may reproduce only non-wallet Production business rules through Replay-local adapters which are version-matched and tested against Production fixtures. It must never claim that it reproduces historical wallet state, live scheduling, MySQL locks, Binance availability, or actual fills.

Release labels are mutually exclusive:

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ANALYSIS_PARITY` | A stored Production signal/outcome is reproducible under the defined as-of evidence and oracle contract. It makes no account/lifecycle claim. |
| `REFUSED_INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE` | Required evidence or lineage is absent, stale, ambiguous, or forbidden. No signal/trade artifact is published. |
| `FAILED_REPLAY` | Internal error/cancellation after staging began. Staged artifacts are discarded. |

Existing FIX-11K, FIX-11Q, pre-FIX-122, and `EXPERIMENTAL` paths remain displayable only; they cannot enter a baseline result.

## 2. Explicit Replay boundary

The boundary is the Regression Replay entry points: `RegressionTestService`, its controllers/requests, `RegressionTestWorker`, `ShadowProductionReplayService`, Replay observers, `/runs/**` output, and every asynchronous child task they start.

They must not read or write any Production account table: `wallet_asset`, `wallet_trade`, `wallet_managed_position`, `paper_position`, `wallet_settings`, account snapshots, daily-account statistics, or live execution state. They must not invoke Binance/HTTP clients or call a Production fallback branch. A run-scoped guard propagates to all Replay child threads and fails closed with `REPLAY_FORBIDDEN_DEPENDENCY` before publication.

`TradeReplayService.replay(positionId)` is an existing Production inspection view, not Regression Replay; it is explicitly outside this boundary and must not be changed by FIX-156.

**Recorded-entry fixtures (review finding F1).** A lifecycle comparison is seeded from Production's recorded entries, which live in the account tables that Replay may not read. The recorded entries therefore reach Replay only as an **immutable entry-fixture dataset**, prepared by a separate read-only extraction that runs outside the Replay execution boundary and is never part of a Replay run. Each fixture holds: symbol, position identifier, recorded entry time, execution price and the observed-at time of that price, the entry signal identifier, the normalised fixed-notional basis (the recorded quantity is kept for audit and is not used for sizing), initial stop loss and take profit, entry scores, entry-consumption state, and the protection state at entry. The dataset has a content hash recorded in the run certificate. Replay reads the fixture file or Replay-owned fixture table only; the forbidden-dependency guard still applies to every account table. The extraction queries and their results are kept as evidence (E09).

## 3. Evidence contract and time model

### 3.1 Allowed evidence

Replay reads only durable market/decision evidence, each with an as-of rule:

| Evidence | Permitted use | Limitation / refusal rule |
|---|---|---|
| `candle` | indicator timeline | exact symbol/interval/open/expected-close identity; decision-time closure lineage required for parity; current `closed=1` alone is not proof. |
| `trade_signal`, `candle_analysis_outcome`, `signal_processing_work` | stored outcome/oracle | compare only fields and signal modes explicitly versioned by Section 7. |
| `market_price_event` | canonical execution/protection price timeline | accept only `LEGACY`/`APPLIED`; retain event id, `observed_at`, ordering slot and status. Coverage is per span, not a run-wide flag. |
| `order_book_snapshot`, `fix122_evaluation`, `buy_htf_assessment_audit`, `execution_opportunity` | diagnostic/context only | best-effort, rollback-surviving, or overwritten evidence cannot prove parity unless an immutable as-of snapshot exists. |
| sentiment/fundamental tables | analysis input only | require collection/availability time and versioned provider/config snapshot; otherwise refuse `ANALYSIS_PARITY`. |

`NON_CANONICAL`, `PROTECTION_NOT_APPLIED`, `PENDING`, and uncertain price events are excluded. No future candle, price, signal, configuration, provider-health value, or account state may be used.

### 3.2 Candle and signal eligibility

For every requested candle, Replay must apply the same 210-closed-candle data-quality rule and validate snapshot identity **after** construction. Expected close is `open_time + interval - 1 ms`. Open, backfill-ambiguous, missing, or identity-mismatched rows refuse parity. BTC and higher-timeframe visibility use the same signal-mode-specific as-of clock as the stored Production decision; if ordering cannot be reconstructed, parity is refused.

Recovery/backfill may make a candle present later. It cannot retroactively prove that it was available to Production at the original decision time.

### 3.3 Price coverage and fill policy

For a comparable decision output, each position-dependent decision span requires fresh accepted price evidence. Source check: Production resolves execution prices (entries and progressive adds) in `ExecutionPriceAuthorityService.resolve`, which accepts a price only if it is no older than `MAX_EXECUTION_PRICE_AGE`, 15 seconds. The Replay-scope branch of the same method applies the same 15-second limit to the Replay price timeline. That rule covers entry and add prices only. E02 must state which freshness rule governs protection (exit) spans, because the protection price stream is filtered by event status, not by this 15-second limit. A span with no usable price event is refused; it is never silently represented by one `EXACT_PRICE_REPLAY` flag for the entire run.

No candle-price fill assumption is part of this parity baseline. A future counterfactual research run may introduce one only under a separately approved design and must not claim parity.

The existing signal-price fallback is removed from the Replay baseline. It is reachable only for runs with **zero** price events, and does not execute the full Production exit order. Tests must use the actual Production signal-path sequence: advisory position management, TP, stop loss, rebase floor, profit lock, normal SELL validation, near-TP, then add suppression/handling as applicable. No rule order may be invented from the old Replay fallback.

### 3.4 Known Production/Replay differences register (source comparison)

Production's price path (`LivePositionProtectionService.onPrice`) and Replay's price path (`evaluateLivePrice`) follow the same exit order. The differences below are in the Production signal path (`PaperTradingService.processSignalBody`), in timing, and in Replay-only logic. Each row must be closed in E02 as **Replay change**, **Production-proven equivalent**, or **declared non-comparable**. Source note: Replay calls the shared `ExecutionIntelligenceService.evaluateBuy` and `TradeExecutionValidationService.validateSell`; it does not carry its own copies. The Replay-local parts are `evaluateExit` (the fallback), the profit-lock state wiring (`profitLockState`, `rebaseForExtendedTarget`), and the position and sizing bookkeeping.

| ID | Difference | Production | Replay (current) | Required disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D01 | SELL signals that can close a position | SELL or STRONG_SELL on 1m, 5m or 1h, through `validateSell` | Only 1m SELL or STRONG_SELL | Replay change |
| D02 | Profit-lock suppression of SELL signals | Active profit lock ignores the SELL and holds | No such check before `validateSell` (confirmed by two independent source reads) | Replay change |
| D03 | Exits at the signal price | Signal path also checks TP, profit lock, stop loss, hard floor at the candle's signal price | Skipped in exact-price mode | Replay change, or proof that the price stream always acts first |
| D04 | TP at signal price | Closes as TAKE_PROFIT directly, no continuation or extension | Not evaluated at signal price | Same as D03 |
| D05 | Signal visibility to the price stream | Newest stored signal at processing time | Visible from `generatedAt` | Measure `created_at` minus `generated_at` per interval; use Production's availability time |
| D06 | Near-TP clock | `Instant.now()` at processing | Price event `observedAt` | One declared rule plus measured outcome impact |
| D07 | Entry price | Fresh price resolved at `Instant.now()` | Resolved at the signal's `generatedAt` | Same as D06 |
| D08 | Entry wake-up | Setup and confirmed-setup wake-ups tried on every signal | Wake-ups only on 5m; 1m goes to `evaluateBuy` | Verify whether the wake-up can fire on 1m; Replay change if so |
| D09 | Progressive adds | Only on 1m and only without an active profit lock (`PaperTradingService`); `evaluateBuy` is not called while the lock is active, so opportunity memory is not touched | No profit-lock check on the add path (confirmed by two independent source reads) | Replay change: skip the add evaluation while the lock is active |
| D10 | Failed mechanical exit | `executeMechanicalExit` can return false and the position stays open | Always exits | Declared non-comparable (wallet-driven) |
| D11 | Near-TP partial harvest skip | Skipped below Binance minimum for the real quantity | Same check, fixed-notional quantity | Declared non-comparable (quantity-driven) |
| D12 | Replay-only logic | None | Zero-event signal-price fallback, FIX-11K and FIX-11Q observers, run-wide exact/fallback boolean | Remove (Section 5.1) |

### 3.5 Signal-generation differences register (source comparison)

Replay and Production both call `AnalysisService.buildSignal`. The differences are in the inputs and the clock passed to it. Each row must be closed in E08 as **Replay change**, **equivalent on fixtures**, or **non-comparable (excluded from the 99% denominator and counted)**.

| ID | Difference | Production | Replay (current) | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S01 | Signal clock | Live `generatedAt` is `Instant.now()` a short time after the candle close; recovery uses the close time | `evaluationTime = open time + interval` | Non-comparable for live-origin rows, or allow a measured latency tolerance |
| S02 | Higher-timeframe and BTC context | Read from the database at processing time; which same-minute signals exist is a race between workers | Read from the Replay timeline; at a given close the 1m always sees the 5m, 1h and BTC signals of that close | Non-comparable; Replay is a deterministic idealisation |
| S03 | Derivatives positioning | Live Binance futures call, not persisted | Historical mode returns unavailable or not applicable; error-path confidence adjustment is -10 in Production and 0 in Replay | Non-comparable |
| S04 | Order book / liquidity | In-memory samples, live fetch when empty | Persisted observations in the window; unavailable when none, where Production returns insufficient-data hold | Equivalent only where persisted sample rate matches the live window; otherwise non-comparable |

| S06 | Data-quality gate | Candle-close worker validates the latest 210 closed candles (gaps, invalid OHLC) and skips the signal; backfilled candles are not analysed | No such gate; Replay analyses every candle in the database | Replay change if row-set parity matters; otherwise report extra rows as non-comparable |
| S07 | Open (unclosed) candles | Only closed candles | The helper that lists candles for the timeline has no closed filter; the dataset loader does filter. Which one feeds the timeline was not fully traced | Verify in E08; Replay change: filter to closed candles |

### 3.6 Comparison trace, ordering, historical configuration and required fixtures

**Availability contract (F4).** Every comparison trace records six timestamps: `candle_close_at`, `signal_generated_at`, `signal_persisted_at`, `signal_available_at`, `decision_evaluated_at` and `price_observed_at`. Each is shown in UTC as stored and with its KSA (+03:00) equivalent. Where `signal_available_at` cannot be reconstructed from stored evidence, the case is classified non-comparable. No timestamp is invented.

**Price-event ordering (F6).** The price query already orders by `(observed_at, id)`, and Replay's later sort by `observed_at` is stable, so equal-time events keep the database order. The projection drops the id, so the order used cannot be audited; Section 6.1 requires the Replay projection to keep it. The team must also establish whether database id order matches Production's processing order. If it does not, equal-timestamp cases cannot claim exact historical ordering and are classified non-comparable.

**Historical configuration gate (F7).** Replacing `wallet_settings` reads with a frozen profile does not reconstruct the settings in force at the original decision. A decision whose governing configuration (profit-lock activation, initial and trail percentages, enable toggles, scoring and context properties) cannot be established for its decision time is classified non-comparable. The current configuration is never substituted silently (E10).

**Required profit-lock suppression fixtures (F3).** The register rows D02 and D09 are closed only with fixtures for: active lock with a 1m SELL; active lock with a 5m SELL; active lock with a 1h STRONG_SELL; active lock with price below the protection floor; active lock with a progressive-add opportunity; and the same cases in the TP-extension rebase state, where the lock is not active and Production does not suppress. The fixtures must show that a mechanical protection exit (price-based lock, stop loss, hard floor) is never suppressed merely because a normal SELL would be.

**Final-tail fixtures (D25).** Lifecycle fixtures must cover, for a position open at the last comparable signal: a stop loss in the tail; a take profit in the tail; a profit-lock exit in the tail; a near-TP outcome in the tail; and an event after `executionEnd`, which must not run. Tail events are processed in canonical `(observed_at, id)` order.

**Per-decision policy fingerprint (F8).** Each comparable decision records the deployed-policy fingerprint (source, configuration and profile hash) in force when Production made it, not only the run-level fingerprint. A decision whose fingerprint cannot be established is non-comparable.

**Data-quality gate as-of (F9).** Replay's reproduction of the 210-closed-candle rule (S06) may use only candles that were historically available at the decision time. Backfilled or recovered candles do not count as available earlier than their persistence time.

**Quantity- and wallet-dependent decisions (F10).** A fixed-notional comparison must not claim equivalence for decisions whose outcome depends on quantity or the wallet, such as the near-TP harvest minimum check (D11), sizing, daily limits and executed-BUY consumption. These are classified non-comparable and counted, never silently matched.

## 4. Frozen Replay profile and fixed-notional output

Every run stores an immutable Replay-owned profile: fixed notional, strategy/exit thresholds, instrument constraints needed by non-wallet decision rules, strategy toggles, FIX-154 policy version, and all version/config fingerprints. It contains no balance, wallet, cash reserve, sizing, daily-loss, or max-open-position state.

The baseline profile mirrors current non-wallet paper-trading rules with fixed notional and current strategy/configuration snapshot. Any Production decision whose outcome depends on cash, daily limits, max-open-position cap, sizing, reserve, or account history is marked `WALLET_DRIVEN_NOT_COMPARABLE`, excluded from the 99% denominator, and counted in the certificate. Production wallet settings are never consulted.

Replay-local mirrors may not add a second strategy engine. Each mirrored method has a named Production source, input/output fixture, policy-version fingerprint, and regression comparison. A source change invalidates the Replay profile until its fixtures and mirror are reviewed.

Their historical rows remain evidence; this change does not delete Production data or edit an applied migration.

**Removal safety rules:** remove invocation and baseline write paths first; migrate/disable UI routes next; retain historical rows and read-only viewers; then consider schema cleanup only in a later approved migration. Never delete a table, archive, or prior run merely to make the new Replay route compile.

## 6. Lifecycle, staging and resources

### 6.1 Required technical change map

| Area | Current technical issue | Required Replay-only change |
|---|---|---|
| `RegressionTestService.start(...)` and run controllers | A run and FIX-122 revision can be written before the async worker qualifies evidence. Chart output can read `wallet_trade`. | Persist only a request/certificate shell at start. Move all result writes after qualification. Route chart/timeline endpoints to Replay-owned output only; prohibit a Replay request from querying `wallet_trade` or `paper_position`. |
| `RegressionTestWorker` | It creates generated artifacts before its late price-evidence check and uses an unspecified `@Async` executor. | Add `ReplayEvidenceQualifier.qualify(request)` before signal/result generation. Use a named bounded Replay executor. Carry profile, baseline hash, mode, scope and cancellation token into the worker. Enforce per-span rather than run-wide price coverage. |
| `ReplayDataset` / candle loading | Replay can process an open row and can re-analyse the preceding closed candle with later context. | Load only exact closed identities. After every indicator snapshot build, compare returned candle symbol, interval, open and expected close with the requested identity. Apply `CandleDataQualityService` semantics as of that decision point. |
| `ExecutionReplayScope` | Scope is a `ThreadLocal`; a missing scope can fall through to Production account reads/writes. It does not carry canonical price identity. | Add immutable run/profile/baseline/clock state, accepted price-event id/status/ordering-slot, cancellation marker and a scope-violation flag. Propagate it to every Replay-owned async task; `finally` clears it. Absence or an attempted account/HTTP dependency raises `ReplayForbiddenDependencyException`. |
| `ShadowProductionReplayService` | It reads `wallet_settings`; `exactPriceReplay` is one run-level boolean; its signal-price fallback runs only when a run has no price events; price path omits some Production exits/lock suppression. | Replace settings with `ReplayProfile`. Replace the boolean with `ReplayPriceCoverage` per decision span. Remove the fallback and use the documented Production-rule mirror order. Never call a repository/service that reads an account table or HTTP. |
| Replay policy mirrors | Production services such as validation, sizing, minimum execution, protection, paper trading and position exit have account/HTTP/transaction dependencies. | Introduce Replay-local `*PolicyMirror` classes with explicit inputs only: immutable profile, as-of market evidence and Replay decision-position state. Wallet-driven decisions are classified `WALLET_DRIVEN_NOT_COMPARABLE`, not mirrored. Each mirror names its Production source method and has recorded-Production-decision fixtures proving equivalent outputs for eligible inputs. No modification of the Production class is allowed. |
| `OneCandleContinuationGraceReplayObserver` and other observers | The observer reads wallet settings and writes experimental output during baseline runs. | Supply the immutable Replay profile; isolate observer writes in Replay tables. Baseline profiles do not instantiate/invoke experimental observers. |
| `ReplayParityValidator` | It compares a small, non-versioned field subset and has no earned-claim/refusal algorithm. | Require a versioned comparison schema, mandatory fields, tolerances, source/config identity, outcome/signal-mode timing, and a structured mismatch certificate. It may award only `ANALYSIS_PARITY`, never lifecycle/account parity. |
| `MarketPriceEventService` projection / Replay price model | The current `PriceEvent` projection loses durable id/status/ordering slot needed for equal-time ordering and audit. | Add a Replay-owned projection/DTO retaining these fields. Do not change ingestion. Query accepted events in `(observed_at, id)` order and record the event id/slot used for every fixed-notional decision/protection evaluation. |
| Sentiment/fundamental/context evidence | Current historical rows do not always retain collection time, provider health/config or immutable context. | Add a qualifier capability matrix. If an input cannot be reconstructed as of the decision time, refuse `ANALYSIS_PARITY`; the run is refused for `ANALYSIS_PARITY`. No substituted input is allowed in the baseline. |
| FIX-154 integration | Source includes higher-timeframe BUY assessment, but historical inputs/audit counters must not be mutated by Replay. | Replay profile carries frozen FIX-154 policy/config identity. Read only the eligible stored evidence. Route counters/audit output to Replay-owned records; prove no Production counter/audit write occurs. |
| Run lifecycle / archive / purge | Current run data can be incrementally visible and run IDs/output references can drift after purge. | Add immutable certificate/profile references, staging ownership key, terminal status, archive state, cancellation reason and retention policy. Promotion is atomic; purge never reuses a public run identity or deletes certificate lineage. |

### 6.2 Required schema and configuration changes

The next verified Flyway migration must be additive and contain, at minimum:

- `replay_profile`: immutable fixed-notional decision-profile configuration, profile hash and source policy version; no balance/ledger fields.
- `replay_run_certificate`: requested/earned label, baseline/config hashes, evidence counts/IDs, refusal/mismatch reasons, UTC timestamps and KSA display conversion metadata.
- Replay staging/promotion ownership columns or dedicated staging tables for every Replay result table.
- `replay_price_coverage`: one row per decision span, recording canonical event identity/order or the refusal reason. No price assumption exists in the baseline.
- Replay-only audit tables for fixed-notional entries/exits, decision positions, policy decisions, experimental observers and FIX-154 equivalent assessment evidence.
- Archive/retention indexes and unique keys that preserve run identity across cancellation/purge.

Configuration must name: the bounded Replay executor, one-run capacity, queue capacity, connection/query budget, maximum window/candle count, supported profile modes, fixed notional, debug decision logging, and the numeric Production-protection health thresholds used by the load test.

1. `start` creates only a minimal run request/certificate record; no FIX-122 revision, signal, trade, observer, or result write occurs before qualification.
2. Qualification takes a read-consistent evidence snapshot and produces qualified spans or a terminal refusal.
3. The worker writes only Replay staging rows. A cancellation, crash, invariant failure, or forbidden dependency discards staging and writes one terminal diagnostic.
4. Promotion publishes all terminal Replay output atomically. Archive/purge preserve certificate/profile/baseline hashes and cannot reuse a run identity.

Use a named, single-worker Replay executor with a bounded queue of one. Specify and test a database connection/query budget. A run is rejected when capacity is full. Under load, Production protection latency and `STALE_PRICE`/non-canonical rates must not worsen beyond an approved numeric threshold.

## 7. Earned parity algorithm

`ANALYSIS_PARITY` is earned only when the frozen source/config policy identity matches, all mandatory as-of evidence exists, candle/data-quality/signal-mode timing passes, and the validator compares the versioned mandatory field set (decision, raw/effective confidence, context/statuses, regime, strategy, entry permission, reason and outcome). Tolerances must be documented and versioned; missing liquidity, derivatives or sentiment uses the stored Production output, not a new live/historical approximation.

The FIX-156 outcome target is **at least 99% agreement among qualified, comparable decisions, measured separately for signal parity and for lifecycle parity (Section 7.1); the two are never pooled**. A unit is one Production-recorded signal decision or position outcome. It passes only when the versioned comparison agrees on entry versus no entry, exit versus hold, exit reason, exit timestamp, and exit price within the frozen tolerance. Wallet-driven cases, insufficient-evidence cases and refused cases are excluded from the denominator and reported separately; none may be counted as a match. Every disagreement has a one-line classified cause. Average P&L is not a substitute for this decision-level metric.

**Validity conditions (frozen before the first measured run):** (a) a minimum coverage, meaning comparable cases as a share of all Production decisions in the window, reported next to the agreement rate; (b) a minimum number of comparable cases; (c) a lower confidence bound on the agreement rate, and the 99% target is judged on that bound, not the raw percentage; (d) the numeric values are set by the team from E06 evidence and approved by the owner. A result that fails (a) or (b) is reported as **not evaluable**, never as a pass.

**Unit of comparison ƒ?" recorded in Appendix C, item 1, awaiting owner confirmation at freeze:** Replay is seeded at Production's recorded entries, so each position's lifecycle is compared from the same entry onward and a wallet-driven BUY rejection in Production cannot cascade into later differences. A free-running lifecycle is not permitted while Replay has no wallet evidence. Appendix C items 2 and 3 also bind this section: thresholds are frozen before the final evaluation window, and D14 is blocking.

### 7.1 Separate acceptance metrics (F2, F5)

| Metric | Compares | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| Signal parity | Production versus Replay signal generation and decision, per Section 3.5 | Own frozen threshold, coverage and lower confidence bound |
| Lifecycle parity | Recorded-entry position management, protection and exit decisions, per Section 3.4 | Own frozen threshold, coverage and lower confidence bound; reported per exit class (stop loss, profit-lock, hard floor, take profit, normal SELL, near-TP) so that a small set of mechanical-exit mismatches cannot hide behind matching signals |
| Overall coverage | Comparable decisions divided by all relevant Production decisions | Frozen minimum, reported next to both rates |

Both parity metrics must meet their own criteria. Every lifecycle mismatch reports the **first divergent decision** (for example a profit-lock update at 10:05 KSA that leads to a different exit at 10:12 KSA), not only the final P&L difference. The first divergence is the defect to investigate.


### 7.2 Critical-safety gate (independent review)

A high overall agreement rate must not hide a protection failure: 990 matching and 10 mismatching decisions is 99%, and if the 10 are stop-loss or profit-lock exits the implementation is rejected. In addition to Section 7.1, the lifecycle comparison must show **zero unexplained critical mismatches** in these classes: stop-loss precedence; profit-lock protection (activation, lock price, trigger, hard floor, SELL suppression); take-profit execution (exit versus extension); FIX-11T near-TP ownership (it acts last and never races another sell or quantity change on the same tick); and duplicate exit authorisation. A critical mismatch counts as explained only when it carries an evidence-based classification (for example non-comparable because the governing configuration cannot be established), reviewed independently. Both the statistical targets and this gate must pass.

The certificate records baseline source hash, deployed-policy/JAR hash when known, config/profile hash, migration range, evidence IDs/counts, per-span price coverage, selected label, refusals, duration, executor utilisation, and UTC/KSA display timestamps. A source/deployed-JAR mismatch prevents a claim about deployed Production.

## 8. Mandatory validation

Tests must cover: account/HTTP/fall-through guard; async guard propagation; open/missing/identity-mismatched/backfilled candle; as-of 210-candle quality; same-boundary BTC/HTF visibility; price id/slot/equal-time ordering; missing/partial price spans; Replay-only SELL versus Production signal-path TP/SL/floor/lock/SELL/add order; profit-lock suppression; wallet-driven exclusion; cancellation/crash/restart/staging/promotion/archive/purge; observer isolation; FIX-154 counters unaffected; API/UI overlay isolation; executor/DB/protection-load limits; MySQL migration fresh/upgrade/V103 policy; and baseline/config hash mismatch.

Before any implementation approval, run bounded read-only measurements for price-event coverage by symbol/day, existing fallback-run count, warm-up sufficiency, and evidence-eligibility rate. If coverage is inadequate, refusal rates must be reported rather than hidden.
